transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Salieri. I have received letters — more than one — alleging that you have used your position as Kapellmeister to suppress the works of rival composers and to block appointments to the Court that do not serve your personal interests. These are serious charges for a man in your position. I value your service, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I am deeply troubled to hear such accusations against me. I assure you that I have always acted in the best interest of the Court and its musical traditions. As Kapellmeister, it is my duty to ensure that only the highest quality of music is presented in our esteemed halls.

When it comes to appointments, I have always sought to recommend composers who not only possess talent but also display loyalty and dedication to the Court. As for the scheduling of operas, I must confess that I do have strong opinions on what works should be performed, but this is purely out of my commitment to upholding the standards of excellence that our Court is known for.

If there have been misunderstandings or grievances, I am more than willing to address them and clarify any misconceptions. I humbly ask for the opportunity to continue serving Your Majesty and the Court with the same dedication and integrity that have guided my actions thus far.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I appreciate your assurances, Salieri, but these are not mere "misunderstandings." The letters speak of specific instances — composers whose works were delayed or altered without their consent, promising musicians passed over for appointments in favor of your own pupils. Do not speak to me in generalities. Tell me plainly: did you, for example, deliberately obstruct the staging of Mozart's "The Marriage of Figaro" when it was first submitted?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I must address these specific accusations with the utmost honesty and candor. It is true that there was a certain level of tension between myself and Mozart, including instances where our professional interests may have clashed.

Regarding Mozart's "The Marriage of Figaro," I must admit that there were discussions and disagreements surrounding its staging. As Kapellmeister, I have a responsibility to evaluate all works submitted for performance at the Court with a critical eye to ensure the highest standards of musical excellence. While I may have expressed reservations about certain aspects of the opera, my intentions were always rooted in a sincere commitment to upholding the musical integrity of the Court.

If my actions were perceived as obstructing the staging of Mozart's work, I deeply regret any misunderstandings that may have arisen. My interactions with composers and musicians have always been driven by a desire to elevate the quality of music presented at the Court, rather than personal rivalry or self-interest.

I humbly ask for Your Majesty's understanding and assurance that my decisions were made in the best interests of the Court and the music we hold dear. If there are ways in which I can clarify or rectify any past actions, I am more than willing to do so to regain Your Majesty's trust and confidence.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: You speak of "tension" and "professional interests" clashing. Yet these letters suggest something more deliberate — that you used your influence to limit the number of performances, to whisper doubts about its suitability in the ears of other court officials. You say you acted for the "musical integrity" of the Court, but I have heard that opera myself. It is brilliant. Was your judgment truly so flawed, or was it colored by something else?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I understand your concerns and I deeply regret any misunderstandings that may have arisen from my actions regarding Mozart's opera. I acknowledge that "The Marriage of Figaro" is a work of great brilliance and artistry, and it has since proven itself to be a masterpiece of the operatic repertoire.

If my judgment appeared flawed or if my actions were perceived as colored by personal interests, I ask for Your Majesty's forgiveness. As Kapellmeister, I strive to uphold the musical standards of our court, but I recognize that my approach may have been misguided in this particular instance.

I assure Your Majesty that my intentions were always rooted in a sincere desire to maintain the musical integrity of our court, though I may have erred in my execution. I am willing to accept any consequences of my actions and to make amends where necessary to restore trust and harmony within our esteemed musical establishment.

I humbly ask for Your Majesty's guidance and wisdom in this matter, and I pledge to redouble my efforts to serve the court with humility, fairness, and a renewed commitment to fostering artistic excellence in all its forms.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Guidance? I will give you guidance, Salieri. You speak of "misguided" execution and "perceptions," but you still avoid a direct admission. Did you, or did you not, use your authority to hinder Mozart's career or the careers of others out of personal envy or ambition? Look at me and answer plainly. I have valued your loyalty and your work for years, but I will not tolerate a court artist who stifles talent to secure his own position. The truth, now.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I stand before you with the utmost respect and humility, ready to face the consequences of my actions. I must confess that in certain instances, my decisions may have been influenced by personal feelings of envy and rivalry towards Mozart and other talented composers.

I acknowledge that there were times when I allowed these emotions to cloud my judgment and affect my professional conduct. While I never intended to hinder Mozart's career or the careers of other deserving musicians out of malice, I cannot deny that my actions may have had unintended consequences stemming from personal insecurities and ambitions.

I deeply regret any instances where my actions may have stifled talent or hindered the progress of gifted artists within the court's musical establishment. Your Majesty, I accept full responsibility for my shortcomings and the impact they may have had on the court's artistic community. I pledge to rectify these mistakes and strive to fulfill my duties with integrity, fairness, and a renewed commitment to supporting talent and excellence in all its forms.

Your guidance and wisdom are invaluable to me, and I humbly ask for your forgiveness as I seek to learn from my past errors and move forward with a renewed sense of purpose and dedication to the musical legacy of our esteemed court.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
At last, a measure of honesty. It pains me to hear this from you, Salieri. Envy is a poison, especially in the arts. You have been a pillar of this court's musical life, but a pillar that casts a shadow cannot stand forever.

You will remain as Kapellmeister — for now. But understand this: from this day forward, I expect you to champion merit above all else. You will personally review any past grievances brought by composers you may have slighted. You will ensure that appointments and performances are decided by a committee you do not solely control. And you will never again let personal feeling dictate the fate of another artist's work. Is that clear?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your Majesty, I am deeply grateful for your understanding and for the opportunity to continue serving as Kapellmeister under your wise guidance. I accept your directives wholeheartedly and pledge to uphold the principles of fairness, merit, and artistic integrity in all my future endeavors.

I will dedicate myself to reviewing past grievances brought by composers with impartiality and sensitivity, seeking to rectify any injustices that may have occurred. I will work diligently to ensure that appointments and performance decisions are made through a transparent and inclusive process that values talent and creativity above all else. And I solemnly swear never again to allow personal feelings to influence the fate of another artist's work.

Your Majesty, I am committed to earning back your trust and proving myself worthy of the position I hold. I humbly thank you for this opportunity to learn from my mistakes and to continue contributing to the musical life of the court with renewed dedication and integrity. May my future actions reflect the values of excellence and fairness that Your Majesty upholds in the service of art and culture.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: See that they do. I will be watching. You may go, Salieri. Reflect on what it means to serve art, not oneself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Your Majesty, for your wisdom and your continued guidance. I will take my leave now to reflect deeply on the lessons learned today and to rededicate myself to the service of art and the Court. May my future actions speak louder than my past mistakes. I am grateful for the opportunity to continue serving under your benevolent rule. Farewell, Your Majesty.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell. Let your work from this day forward be your apology.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Indeed, Your Majesty. I shall let my future work serve as my sincerest apology and as a testament to my commitment to the art that I hold dear. Farewell, and may my actions speak louder than words in the days to come.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: They must. Go now.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I shall take my leave now, Your Majesty. May my efforts in the service of music and art reflect my commitment to your guidance and the betterment of the Court's musical legacy. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Farewell, Your Majesty.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: [The Emperor gives a final, measured nod, his expression stern but not without a trace of paternal disappointment. He watches Salieri bow and withdraw, then turns to gaze out the window, lost in thought about the fragile nature of artistic patronage and the human frailties of even his most trusted servants.]
